event_specific_evidence: USGS tectonic summary places the event in distributed deformation of the Shan-Thai block; focal mechanism indicates potential left-lateral slip on a northeast-trending nodal plane.
caveats: Do not infer a named causative fault from the nodal plane alone. The event is about 400 km east of the Sagaing Fault according to the USGS summary.

event_specific_evidence: EGU abstract identifies right-lateral movement on the Sagaing Fault; Myanmar Earthquake Committee contemporaneously links event to Sagaing activity; World Bank report summarizes the 2012 rupture as about 45 km of the Sagaing segment between Singu and Sabeanago.
caveats: Do not treat the EGU abstract's preliminary 60–70 km rupture estimate as a final geodetic rupture length. A reviewed event-specific moment tensor/fault-plane product should be captured in the project evidence register.

event_specific_evidence: USGS describes strike-slip faulting in the complex India–Eurasia boundary region, near 50 km depth within India-plate lithosphere, and says the causative fault is unknown. Gahalaut & Kundu (2016) explicitly interpret it as an intra-slab event in the Indo-Burmese wedge.
caveats: Retain the source interpretation as a literature-supported candidate, not settled ground truth. The published paper and USGS catalog summary emphasize different aspects; do not attribute it to a specific mapped fault.

event_specific_evidence: Aung et al. (2019) identify the 13 April 2016 Kani Mw 6.9 event as one of two 2016 Myanmar intra-slab events. USGS preferred reviewed W-phase moment tensor has centroid depth 140.5 km and 97% double-couple, with reverse/oblique nodal-plane rakes.
caveats: Catalogue hypocentral depth is 136 km; the USGS W-phase centroid depth is 140.5 km. These are different parameters and must remain separately labelled. A geometry-specific slab-relative depth calculation is not performed here.

event_specific_evidence: Shiddiqi et al. (2018) conduct an event-specific source study and describe the Chauk earthquake as an intermediate-depth intraslab event (about 90 km in their source analysis) with a thrust mechanism. Aung et al. (2019) also group Chauk among the two 2016 Myanmar intraslab earthquakes.
caveats: Frozen catalogue hypocentral depth is 82 km. Do not overwrite it with the source-study depth near 90 km; preserve each estimate with source and parameter type.

event_specific_evidence: USGS preferred reviewed W-phase moment tensor is strike-slip (NP1 1/82/-174; NP2 270/84/-8). USGS finite-fault product and peer-reviewed Science paper identify a roughly 475 km rupture of the Sagaing Fault; USGS 2026 publication describes shallow dextral faulting and surface rupture.
caveats: USGS catalogue hypocentre is 10 km, while W-phase centroid is 40.5 km. These are not interchangeable. The 2025 rupture paper is strong evidence for parent-system assignment, not a full regional boundary polygon.

event_specific_evidence: USGS ComCat records Mww 6.7 at 06:32:04 UTC, 11 min 12.062 s after the Mww 7.7 mainshock. The 2025 BSSA analysis reports an Mw 6.7 aftershock about 11 min after the mainshock, with GCMT centroid depth 19.1 km and dip 73 degrees. The 2026 aftershock study finds the sequence spatially controlled by the north–south Sagaing Fault.
caveats: Frozen ComCat epicentres give 35.023 km separation; a 2025 ComCat snapshot table reports about 32 km, while the BSSA paper reports about 59 km south. Keep the location-solution discrepancy explicit. Do not assign sequence roles or merge event IDs in this regional-adjudication step.
